focus: -ly ending /li/ (quickly, slowly) · /θ/ in health, teeth, mouth · /f/ (cough) & /t/ (walked) in body words · adverb stress placement · irregular 'well' /wel/ vs 'good'
focus_ar: نهاية -ly، و /θ/ في health/teeth، وأصوات كلمات الجسم، ونبر ظرف الحال، و 'well' مقابل 'good'
arabic_challenge: The -ly adverb ending is a weak /li/ that learners often stress or turn into 'lay'. Health and body vocabulary is full of /θ/ (health, teeth, mouth, throat), which Arabic learners may replace with /t/ or /s/.

isolation.instructions: The adverb ending -ly is a weak, quick /li/: QUICK-ly, SLOW-ly, CARE-ful-ly. The stress stays on the adjective part; -ly just tags on lightly. Do not say 'quick-LY' or 'quick-lay'.
isolation.instructions_ar: نهاية الظرف -ly خفيفة وسريعة /li/: QUICK-ly. النبر يفضل على الصفة و -ly تتلزق بخِفّة. مش 'quick-LAY'.

daily_drills.record_this: Please speak slowly and clearly so I can understand. He drives very carefully, and she finished the test quickly and easily.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'quickly'. Is -ly a light /li/ tag, with the stress on 'QUICK'?

isolation.instructions: Health and body words are full of /θ/: health, teeth, mouth, throat, thumb, thigh. Tongue tip between the teeth, NO voice, air flows. Do not use /t/ or /s/.
isolation.instructions_ar: كلمات الصحة والجسم مليانة /θ/: health, teeth, mouth, throat. طرف اللسان بين الأسنان، بدون صوت، والهوا مستمر.

sentence_practice: Brush your teeth for good health.
My throat hurts and I feel thin.
daily_drills.record_this: Brush your teeth twice a day for good health. Open your mouth and say 'ah'. My throat hurts a little, and I need to take a deep breath.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'teeth' and 'health'. Is your tongue visible between your teeth for /θ/?

isolation.instructions: Health verbs bring back earlier sounds: cough /kɒf/ (silent 'gh' → /f/!), walked /wɔːkt/, rest /rest/, breathe /briːð/ (voiced th!). Note 'cough' ends in /f/, and 'breathe' ends in voiced /ð/.
isolation.instructions_ar: أفعال الصحة بترجّع أصوات قديمة: cough تنتهي بـ /f/ (gh صامتة)، و breathe تنتهي بـ /ð/ مجهورة.

sentence_practice: I have a cough and a sore throat.
My head aches and I feel sick.
daily_drills.record_this: I have a bad cough and a sore throat. The doctor said to breathe deeply, take some medicine and rest. My head aches and I feel a little sick.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'cough'. Does it end in /f/ (like 'off'), with no /g/ sound?

isolation.instructions: Adverbs of manner usually come after the verb/object and are lightly stressed: 'He speaks English FLU-ently', 'She runs QUICK-ly'. The main verb keeps the strongest stress.
isolation.instructions_ar: ظروف الحال بتيجي بعد الفعل/المفعول وبتتنبر بخِفّة. الفعل الرئيسي يحتفظ بأقوى نبر.

sentence_practice: She works hard and sleeps well.
daily_drills.record_this: He speaks English fluently and writes carefully. She works hard all day and usually sleeps well. Please drive slowly and carefully in the rain.
daily_drills.self_check: Note: 'works hard' (a lot) is different from 'hardly works' (almost none). Did you mean the right one?

isolation.instructions: 'Good' is the adjective (a good doctor); 'well' is the adverb (she sings well) AND means 'healthy' (I feel well). 'Well' uses /w/ + short /e/ + /l/ — do not say 'wall' or 'will'.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'good' صفة و 'well' ظرف (sings well) وتعني كمان 'بصحة جيدة'. 'well' فيها /w/ + /e/ + /l/ — مش 'wall' ولا 'will'.

sentence_practice: She is a good doctor and she explains well.
He plays well but he trained badly.
daily_drills.record_this: She is a very good doctor and she explains everything well. I don't feel well today — I have a cough. He plays football well, but last week he trained badly.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'well'. Is it clearly /wel/, not 'will' or 'wall'?

challenge_sentences: Brush your teeth carefully for good health.
I don't feel well — I have a cough and a sore throat.
daily_drills.record_this: Brush your teeth carefully every day for good health. I don't feel well today — I have a bad cough and a sore throat. The doctor speaks slowly and clearly. She told me to breathe deeply and rest well.
daily_drills.self_check: Three checks: weak -ly, dental /θ/ in health words, and 'well' vs 'good' used correctly.

test_yourself.instructions: Record yourself talking about health and habits. Then listen back and check each feature.
test_yourself.instructions_ar: سجّل نفسك وانت تتكلم عن الصحة والعادات، وبعدين اسمع وراجع كل نقطة.
test_yourself.passage: To stay healthy, I try to live carefully. I eat slowly, brush my teeth twice a day, and sleep well every night. I usually feel well, but last week I wasn't good — I had a bad cough and a sore throat, and my head ached badly. The doctor spoke to me calmly and clearly. She told me to breathe deeply, rest quietly and drink plenty of water. She's a very good doctor and she explains everything well. Now I feel much better. I've learnt that if you look after your health carefully, your body works well.

sounds_to_check.-ly = weak /li/: carefully, slowly, calmly, clearly, quietly, badly
sounds_to_check.adverb placement: eat SLOWLY, sleep WELL, ached BADLY, explains WELL
sounds_to_check.'well' vs 'good': feel well, sleep well, a good doctor, explains well

scoring_guide.90_100: -ly is light, /θ/ dental, and 'well/good' used correctly. A2 phonology is solid — ready for week 11.
scoring_guide.50_69: 'teeth' → 'teet', or good/well confused. Repeat days 2 and 5.
scoring_guide.below_50: Redo days 1-5, watching the tongue for /θ/ and keeping -ly light.

for_arabic_speakers: -ly is a weak tag (/li/), never stressed and never 'lay'.
You have ث — use it for health, teeth, mouth, throat.
'cough' ends in /f/; 'breathe' (verb) ends in voiced /ð/, 'breath' (noun) in /θ/.
'good' is the adjective, 'well' the adverb: 'she sings well', not 'sings good'.
supplementary_notes.recording_requirement: Record the 'record_this' line daily; compare day 7 with day 1.
